elements.text:
Upgrade to boost 1.72, current secp256k1, zeromq and consensus sources, as well as removal of qrencode, png and zlib dependencies has been merged. NuGet packages for secp256k1 have been uploaded, though I'm not intending to update NuGet for zeromq.

Instead I'm planning to move to vcpkg, which is c++ oriented and includes more current boost packages, and includes well-maintained zeromq packages. secp256k1 packaging continues to be a problem as the library is not versioned, so I'll end up building (only) and maintaining a package for it.

Once this is complete I will create vs2019 project files and remove generation and testing of vs2013 (vc120/c++11 CTP).

There are Travis breaks on all macOS builds due to a Travis change affecting boost installation. I'm going to resolve this next, and add builds for the Travis big-endian and Windows platforms. Also on the build roadmap is generation for mingw builds and VS code projects for all three platforms.

elements.text: Bitcoin is a tree index of headers, and blocks are indexes of txs per header. The data all has two levels of validation. Static validation is structural, and independent of any external state. Contextual validation is relations to other elements. The tree can be built with static and limited contextual validation (blocks to each other and txs to blocks). This relies on work to give storage a cost.

elements.text: When you build the tree you ask each peer for its headers using an exponentially backed-off index of your own. The peer will send its headers starting at the highest known common block. This is standard p2p behavior. We do not want to allow a subset of peers determine the chain, so these requests are promiscuous. And there is no prioritization but response time (unlike block download) apart from the configured peer timeouts, since we also don’t want to let fast peers determine the chain. All peers compete to built the tree, and the set of headers that a peer has is not knowable until they are received. So if all peers are in sync there will be up to N times duplicate headers. This doesn’t always happen in practice since the fastest responder causes subsequent requests to have higher common points.

text:
Hello guys!

So I was checking bn’s code and I noticed that `close()` needs to be called from the main thread.
Inside full_node’s code it leads me to check “join”. But I don’t understand what is “join” a reference to.
Could you help me understand that?
```// Close must be called from main thread.
if (node_->close())

// This must be called from the thread that constructed this class (see join).
bool full_node::close()```

elements.text: Join refers to the thread join. The process cannot terminate until threads are all coalesced, which join waits on.

text: Join refers to the thread join. The process cannot terminate until threads are all coalesced, which join waits on.

elements.text: A threadpool thread cannot call close, since it will then deadlock as it is waiting on itself. That’s why the comment is there.
